profile.reading: This is CSC IT Center for Sciences data center in Kajaani, in the Kainuu region of central Finland, built inside a converted former UPM-Kymmene paper mill warehouse. CSC, a Finnish state owned non-profit that provides high performance computing services to universities and research institutions across the country, worked with Finnish architecture and engineering firm Sweco to transform the roughly 200 meter long industrial building, whose renovated facade combines corrugated steel panels in different colors with CorTen weathering steel intended to echo the red brick industrial architecture typical of the surrounding area. The facility runs entirely on hydroelectric power and recovers waste heat from its cooling systems to warm the incoming air supply for its own office spaces, part of a broader Kajaani Data Center Ecosystem that has grown around CSCs presence in the city, drawing further high performance computing tenants to the same industrial site. CSC itself was established in 1971 and is owned by the Finnish state and Finnish higher education institutions, administered under the countrys Ministry of Education and Culture as a non-profit organization headquartered in Espoo. Beyond the Kajaani facility, CSC provides supercomputers, database and information servers, data storage and archival services to Finnish academia and research institutions, and separately operates FUNET, Finlands national research and education network, connecting universities and research organizations across the country. This building sits within the wider Kajaani Data Center Ecosystem, an industrial cluster that has also drawn LUMI, one of Europes fastest supercomputers, which CSC operates on behalf of the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking from a separate building on the same former paper mill site, though LUMI is tracked in this directory as its own distinct facility rather than part of this CSC building.
